reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) supports that DeepMD potentials trained via active learning on AIMD data can model solid and liquid states of a refractory high-entropy carbonitride, but it does not provide any evidence comparing such potentials to EAM references, nor does it address phase-space overlap or thermodynamic integration mismatch. The key premises about improved representation over EAM and the resulting reduction in integration path mismatch are therefore unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: DeepMD potentials can be trained on AIMD data for refractory multicomponent systems to achieve high accuracy.
Active learning (DP-GEN) iteratively incorporates diverse solid and liquid configurations into the training set.
A deep learning potential trained this way will better represent disordered liquid configurations than conventional EAM potentials.
Better representation of liquid configurations increases phase-space overlap between reference and target in thermodynamic integration.
Increased phase-space overlap reduces the thermodynamic integration path mismatch.
